newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador central bank sees 1.3 pct May inflation.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador central bank sees 1.3 pct May inflation.

text.p: The head of Ecuador's central bank, Fidel Jaramillo, said late Tuesday he expects May's monthly inflation to come in around 1.3 percent, slowing from a 2.04 percent rise in April.
"We expect inflation for this month to come in about 1.3 percent, in line with our forecasts," Jaramillo said at a conference.
Cumulative inflation for the past 12 months, meanwhile, should come in at 30.5 percent in May, the central bank director said.
The government is hoping to close 1997 with annual inflation of around 30 percent, and then estimates a drop to between 20 to 23 percent the following year.
Cumulative inflation in the first four months of the year came to 14 percent compared with 11.1 percent in the same period a year earlier.
At the end of 1996, annual inflation stood at 25.53 percent, up from 22.8 percent in 1995.
